pages:
He mansplained me feminism
It was late when I set this date with a delivery man and I was video chatting with my mother on the giant monitor in the living room that wasn't mine but my roommates. My mother wanted to meet my date who arrived: tall, and in a leather jacket.
There was a bar only a few blocks from my house that I rarely frequented, despite its proximity. There was a park on the other side of it. We ordered drinks for ourselves and chose a high two person table overlooking the park. It seemed we had a lot in common as we'd both studied the same subject in college but rather than compare our experiences he used this - the fact that I was supposedly interested in the subject - as a launchpad to tell me all about his experience, including things I'd learned in my intro class.
Blech. I was bored. In spite of myself I could not figure out how a situation that had seemed so promising - he was tall, attractive and dorky to boot, we were getting beers at a bar near my house - had suddenly turned into an opportunity to explain every detail of a class trip he'd gone on with his hilarious trip leader Ralph, master of hijinx...even so I listened on, unsure how to politely steer the conversation away from this veritable hell.
Afterwards we walked around nearby. It was dark and late and a little bit spooky at night. We'd arrived at another park, or perhaps the same one from the other side when he decided to explain his policies regarding feminism.
"Women are always getting hit on by guys when they don't want to be. Honestly, I feel bad for them. They could just be enjoying a day at the park, sitting alone reading, and suddenly there's a swarm of guys who think it's their personal business..." I supposed this was true but hoped to interject a bit more nuance to the situation.
To be honest, this hadn't happened to me very often, and I for one loved talking to strangers. I felt a bit sorry that he was recounting an experience I hadn't had for me and wished he would only give a little bit of my opinion that I might convince him this wasn't supremely true. In a sense I felt that what he was saying was that women couldn't quite handle themselves in public; they weren't equipped to say no to guys that wanted their number, and he felt sorry for the poor dears who had to field off requests from men like a spartan in a cage of lions.
as when I tried to speak, he sort of talked over me. He just couldn't seem to get past this one-sided picture of the woman minding her own business, say in the park or a public library, when suddenly, from out of nowhere, not 2 but three or four men attack her with their kind words and compliments, refusing to take no for an answer.
Now I consider myself a fairly attractive girl but this has never been my experience. Sure I've been asked out by the odd man or two but never a tall good looking guy like himself. In spite of himself, I felt like advising him to try just once or twice, for the sake of the women in my neighborhood, sitting alone in the park, waiting for someone too....I tried to make the point
I felt like saying: "if she's sitting in the park reading, she probably wants to be asked out. If she didn't want to, she could just stay home by herself."
I gave up on trying to say anything, realizing he'd literally just mansplained feminism to me
After this he came home and he didn't want to stay over. This was an undeniably strange turn of events. I couldn't tell if he thought I didn't want him to stay. In any event, he put on one last youtube video which was the theme song to the show "too many cooks" which, if you haven't seen it, goes on and on. At this point I was so done with the date that I simply told him enough was enough and that I hadn't bargained for this hour and a half long video. He left shortly after and we didn't speak again.

name: Paul
dek: After the sixth long phone call with Tyler.
pages:
After my sixth long phone conversation with Tyler, I called one of my potential dates that I’d neglected to follow up on after they’d texted me after I’d given them my number in hopes that we could talk on the phone. He told me that he’d just gotten home from watching a movie by himself and that before that he’d gone to the park and swung on the swings by himself.
We talked about online dating and he said for him it was sad and disappointing and we agreed that meeting after messaging online took the spontaneity out of meeting potential partners. He said he’d gone one a few dates and they’d all gone horrendously bad or the people had been boring and he had or hadn’t followed up with them, that sometimes he’d followed up with them only because he wanted friends to hang out with because he was bored. He lived with two boys – his brothers, and they were all in a band together. He’d spent the day in the recording studio. I told him that he and his brothers were probably secretly the Jonas Brothers.
He said the movie he’d seen had been a chick flick but that he’d liked it a lot and that it made him feel something and that people liked movies that made them feel things.
He said that he often watched movies by himself and though it seemed like an undesirable situation, he enjoyed spending time by himself a lot.
He said his brothers had moved to Portland after he’d left home and I said that he was secretly Nick Jonas from the Jonas Brothers and why hadn’t he told me that before, when we’d been talking on the dating website.
We decided to meet the next day for me to give him the art lesson. He came the next day after 4:00 and we sat down at the wooden table and I was all frantic and upset after having had nothing to eat the entire day.
I was talking a lot and fast it seemed and I was trying to calm myself down but I felt I had low energy and low ability to be pleasant and calm since I was food deprived. I had planned a lesson for him based on the book “Drawing on The right Side of the Brain” by Betty Edwards so I gave him the shell to draw and he described its surface as I asked him to do and then he took down the details on the paper.
I was impressed with how much he’d captured and he said he felt that it was a very poor attempt. I said it wasn’t fair for him to degrade his own performance like that, and that I was being genuine in saying that it was good. I was a little jealous, even, since he’d had so little training.
I lectured him about observing things carefully and how you were supposed to do something and how art wasn’t about the finished product but about altering your vision. I had him draw a gesture of me with my head on the table; the pose was inspired by feeling dead. His drawing was very good and he drew my hair and the lower half of my body and everything and it was scribbly and squiggly and once again I tried to convince him that it really was an excellent work of art.
He did a contour drawing of something else without looking. After we had done everything, he drew a maze that was born out of a drawing of my phone that I’d been holding. Then he went back and labelled all the drawings and drew himself being abducted by a flying saucer in his first shell drawing and added some flowers to the maze one and added captions and titles to all of them.
I felt like I was not standing on anything, I had no idea where to go with the art lesson, he refused to acknowledge his talent and I had not been prepared for him to already understand the basis of conceptual art and felt strange about shifting gears after I’d provided this basis of a solid foundation for our lesson based on the assumption that people were all dumb and didn’t know anything and couldn’t think for themselves.
I felt that I’d failed myself by not teaching him what he wanted to know and he seemed to be frustrated or at least tuned out of our date. I took some pictures of him with his drawings and he told me I should keep them and that I could send him pictures of them.
He said he was going to a show that was nearby and I asked if I could come if I finished my game night early and he didn’t seem especially enthusiastic about me coming but we figured out where it was together anyway on his map on his phone and he played trying to guess where the venue was (it was at a pizza place?) without typing in the address on google maps but gave up and typed it in anyway and it was where he had just gotten to with moving his finger along the roads.
I promised him I’d send him pictures of his drawings. He told me a bit about the place that he worked and I apologized for making him come all the way to my house for the short art lesson. His coworker had texted him that she had forgotten her keys and she needed to close the shop and so he had to drive back to where he worked and give her the keys.
Right before he stood up to leave, he said “Would you like to get a beer sometime?” and I couldn’t tell if his strange voice when he said that was because he was nervous about what I would say or because he didn’t necessarily actually want to or something completely different. I agreed excitedly as I hadn’t been sure that this date was going well at all, and especially not wanting to ruin my near perfect streak, and he left.
I neglected to text him the pictures and instead sent him a message saying “I never sent you the pictures” and then a wall of a few dozen emojis which he completely ignored.
(We talked on the phone the night before about how he'd gone to a movie by himself and playing music in a band and he agreed to come over for an art lesson. The next day I didn't eat at all and then I was starving when he got there which made it hard to communicate or behave positively or concentrate on the impression I might be giving him in any regard. We sat at the table in the living room and I showed him how to do certain things with his pencil or he showed me since he was unequivocally better at drawing than me even though he'd never tried.)

name: Jasper
dek: A friend from the Rocky Horror crowd, two a.m.
pages:
I made a friend in the crowd that streamed out of the Rocky Horror Picture Show when it ended at the ungodly hour of two am. He led me back to one of his friend’s houses, where we proceeded to drink and talk, with the constant presence of a large gray bulldog, who probably weighed more than me and was, to be honest, making me very nervous. The two friends I had made left abruptly and I was left in the house of this stranger, and his dog, but rather than asking me to leave, he seemed complacently friendly, perhaps happy to have the company, certainly excited to have a willing audience for his impromptu obedience class; he told me to grip the ears and if the dog didn't listen to me, to climb on top of it and hold its ears down to show it who was boss.
I didn't really feel like doing that right then, I wasn't in a bossy mood, but I was intimidated by Jasper and the prospect of staying at his house even though I didn't know him so I tried my best to follow his instructions. But I sort of just wanted to make friends with the dog and to have Jasper teach him discipline. He was curiously invested in my progress and assumed that I was similarly invested.
We went upstairs with the dog who I had begun calling "Kitty," and I sat in his black leather chair that was directly in front of a massive stereo system as he played different records and cds. We eventually got tired and smoked weed and decided we should go to bed if we planned on getting food with his friends in the morning. I was having all sorts of anxious but interesting thoughts, having gotten high for the first time in so long and was engrossed in them, was thinking something magical as I sat there in the black chair, was analyzing every aspect of my interaction with him, whether to make eye contact etc. Even though I was barely talking; I asked him about some of the records he'd put on, feigning a bit more knowledge of music then I really had.
He said that he worked in sound and often went record shopping and had found the records but had yet to listen to them even though he'd bought them a long time ago. We went to bed and the dog fell asleep right in between us, though we were just barely touching hands as we drifted off. In the morning we went to a few different places, we walked around, we got coffee, we went to my house, we went to a bar that he frequents, my feet were tired from walking and my shoes were pretty uncomfortable, they were the Harley Davidson motorcycle boots and I wasn't wearing socks.
The strangest thing that happened perhaps was when we got back to my house. Ostensibly, this would be my time to say goodbye, seeing as I had a house, and I’d been staying at his only out of convenience. Instead, this was not even mentioned. It’s unclear whether the thought of leaving me home did not occur to him; instead it remained one of many errands, no different than the rest. It seemed I belonged with him, not in any dramatic sort of way, only in the way of camaraderie between two people who have suddenly come to share a living situation. There was no comment.
The dog came with us of course and a lot of our interaction was based on talking to the dog, or him telling me about it. I asked him questions about it. I reflected on my overwhelming desire in this situation for this interaction to be pleasant and devoid of negative feelings, which was resulting in my not talking about myself at all, not disclosing much of my personality whatsoever, and listening with feigned enthusiasm, to whatever it occurred to him to tell me.
I was also intent, perhaps, on continuing this strange encounter for as long as it might go on for. There was no end in sight. I felt any hint of my personhood might alert him to the fact that he was now harboring a second person. No, the safest way was to remain faceless, nameless, boring, uninteresting, numb.
At the bar he ordered some kind of food and I ordered a beer after a bit of deliberation and talking to the waitress about it a lot. His friends called him and said that they were nearbyish so we took the bus to the place that they were and I fell asleep in my seat for a minute.
His friends consisted of a male, about 30, who he'd known for a long time it seemed, the male's sister, and the male's wife. The male's wife was wearing, I think, a very elegant sun hat and they started taking pictures in front of this guy's jeep that had parked right in front of us except the wheels were huge so maybe it was actually a monster truck.
He and his sister swapped clothes and texted a picture of them to their mother. I couldn't understand the relationship between the sister and the wife completely. We ordered more drinks and there was a whole thing with the bill - the wife was complaining to the waitress that she'd charged too much, the wife was supposed to foot the whole bill, I didn't understand why, perhaps she’d been treated in the past? The dynamics of the situation fell through the slats in my tired mind.
There was a little questions about how Jasper and I knew each other and some reminiscence about how Jasper and the male knew each other. I felt like Jasper didn't quite know how to navigate the social situation and I, for one, didn’t either. He told a few longish stories that were met with an unenthusiastic response. We all walked back to their house and the guy barbequed some stuff in the side yard.
Their apartment was very nice, everything was white, it seemed expensive. We went and sat at the picnic table in the back. The wife and sister were engrossed in a conversation and ignored me. There was something about the food - I wasn't hungry or it didn't taste good. The girls were making fun of the boy for keeping on bringing out more and more food even though ostensibly no one was extremely hungry.
I got in a conversation with the man and it felt a lot better than the conversations intermittently I'd been having with the two women who reminded me of everyone I'd gone to high school with. Nevertheless, I enjoyed witnessing their burgeoning female bond and noting the things it seemed to be based on though I felt distinctly that I could not participate in it.
Eventually, Jasper and I walked home and after we got home we relaxed and watched a comedy show - Sarah Silverman probably - some girl making lots of semi-funny jokes that I was engrossed in, thinking about women comics etc. and then we finally settled on watching Trainspotting which was great and I'd never seen it before. We were cuddling on the couch and it was sweet and very cozy even though he seemed to be in a strange position. Eventually we went upstairs and went to bed and made out a little and he ran his hands over my body but didn’t take any of my clothes off. The dog came bounding onto the bed, though, and our excursion ended. In the morning, we said goodbye on the platform between the stairs, unsure of what sort of closeness had been fostered, and therefore what sort of goodbye might be appropriate. The sun was streaming in through the window above, making the stairs are dappled and sunny. Perhaps he took my hand - I cannot think what happened.
and he didn’t seem like he was trying to get rid of me at all, in fact, he seemed a little sad that I was leaving. I said vaguely that we would see each other again, and perhaps exchanged phone numbers.

My house seeming purple and pink, me bending forward to attach my laces to themselves to each other and to seem like I was occupied and busy – to seem like there was something I was going to do – I was a king masquerading as a queen. Everything was compiled in the rim of a pair of see-through glasses.
Through the royal threshold that led between the dining room and the kitchen I moved, being flippant and adding some politeness as an afterthought.
He went with me between the rooms and went with me between the jokes I was making, following at a reasonable distance.
He hovered at the edge of the wooden kitchen table and I came to stand next to him and almost touch him. He flicked himself away to stand slightly to the left so my experiment to see whether I could initiate a physical connection without the preamble of the date had failed.
As I made my way around that little space of the kitchen, I began to feel faint. I overwhelmingly didn't want to pretend, or make small talk and I wondered if I could simply refuse. I found myself standing on the step above him and was at about his height. I decided to move my head the two inches it would take to reach his. But I didn't do it. He led the way outside to his car which was white and notably not falling apart. It seemed like a sports car but I don't know anything about sports cars. There was something about the front engine that screamed class and that it had taken a little bit of money to buy it.
We went inside the car and I note that he had a watch on his wrist and therefore was not exactly a hipster. It also had hair; so he felt like a man.
I was at my desk in the computer room when their appeared a face with brown hair on top of it in the pane of glass that is part of the door, casually. I figured that he was waiting for me to come get him for the date that we'd arranged beforehand so I walked away from my silver computer to open the door for him even though I was still working on the metaphysical theory I’d been engrossed in before this young man came to my house in the middle of the day for what seemed like no particular reason except that there existed a thread of digital communication which had made it occur.
He told me about his job, at evergreen. We got out of the car, we went into the restaurant. I pulled out my wallet to pay for my beer. It wasn’t that he had it was that I hadn’t and so they were black and so things were good.
He brought us tall brown bottles of beer that had a red label and white inside of that. We drank them. Pretty fast. I lolled at the table, turning brown – the same color as the dark side of the beer bottles that rolled down from the liquid inside of them.
It seemed unlikely to do anything and while he was in the bathroom I pulled out white note cards that I was in the habit of bringing with me. And we drew ideas for things that we could do that day. We both had a card that said "tell something horrible that happened to you" and his had the addendum that it should not be too terrible.
He said it was because he didn't want us to start talking about our dead parents. I told him about the night before where I had been stumbling around drunk by myself for literally the entire night. And I’d lost my backpack. Somehow I doubted he'd ever been involved in something so silly, and so stupid, but he told me one night he'd fallen asleep on some grass somewhere outside a bar, woken up after it was closed, and walked to his house and got there when the buses started running. He said he always sometimes went to sleep in the day as the buses would rumble up outside his window every 20 minutes. He would sometimes scream at them.
The cards turning white that we were playing on – the two tinges – the flashes of the perked up white that is to come.
He leaves to get us another beer. The guy at the table in front of us looks at me “It sounds like you guys are having a very interesting conversation. Is it a first date?” I reply yes.
When he returned, we began speaking about art. A common interest, it seemed. He began explaining his artistic process involved creating a digital work, and then printing out the picture, but then deleting the digital file. I understood that this meant that while his work had most of the qualities of being digital, it wasn’t automatically reproducible, and I wondered if this made it more rare for him.
In spite of myself, I was impressed with his courage to delete a digital file, and my mind thought of all sorts of alternatives (saving it on a usb, just telling people it was deleted), before I remembered this was the exact point of the work.
I wanted him to know that I knew what he was explaining, without him having to even say it.
Stunned that he was still explaining what I already knew I tried to magically ooze myself between his words like bubble syrup explaining that I could say the same thing that he was saying to me to him.
“You see? You get it?” Yes I saw, yes I got it. No oozing allowed.
Dear Adam I’m sorry, this is true, this is just what happened.

I could feel myself slipping, lying down on the fuzzy carpet that was between us, just falling into the ball pit, letting myself get shot at the shooting range, collapsing. I couldn’t explain the silences like I usually could, I let them get to me.
